episodes.name: Oil shock and Nifty-Fifty bust, 1973-74
episodes.cause: The oil embargo, high inflation and Fed funds rising from 3.5% to 13% hit stretched Nifty-Fifty valuations as Bretton Woods collapsed.
episodes.notes: A hiking Fed and stretched valuations before the embargo; Nasdaq depth is approximate.

episodes.name: Volcker rate shock, 1980-82
episodes.cause: Volcker's hikes to 19-20% caused a double-dip recession with unemployment reaching 10.8%.
episodes.notes: Policy rates near 20% and an inverted curve; the first dip (Jan - Jul 1980) came before this peak; Nasdaq depth is approximate.

episodes.name: Black Monday crash, 1987
episodes.cause: Rates up 300 bp in 1987, dollar tension after the Louvre accord and portfolio insurance turned stretched valuations into a one-day 20.5% fall.
episodes.notes: No recession warning; stretched valuations and a Fed hiking into a high market.

episodes.name: Gulf War oil shock, 1990
episodes.cause: Iraq's invasion of Kuwait doubled the oil price on top of the savings and loan crisis and a credit crunch.
episodes.notes: Tightening bank lending standards and the S&L credit crunch before the oil shock.

episodes.name: Russia default and LTCM, 1998
episodes.cause: The Asian crisis, Russia's default on August 17 and the LTCM collapse; the Fed cut three times.
episodes.notes: No recession signal; a brief curve inversion (a false alarm) and credit spreads gapping; -22% intraday.

episodes.name: Dot-com bust, 2000-02
episodes.cause: Dot-com valuations (CAPE 44), Fed funds to 6.5% and a capex bust, then 9/11 and the Enron and WorldCom frauds.
episodes.notes: Extreme valuation, a hiking Fed, an inverted curve and breadth that broke a year before the index.

episodes.name: Global financial crisis, 2007-09
episodes.cause: The housing bust and subprime losses at leveraged banks ended in the Lehman failure and a credit freeze.
episodes.notes: An inverted curve in 2006-07, permits down over 20% a year, tighter lending standards and widening credit spreads.

episodes.name: US downgrade and euro crisis, 2011
episodes.cause: The US credit downgrade on August 5, the debt-ceiling fight and the euro sovereign crisis.
episodes.notes: No recession signal; VIX term structure inverted and credit spreads widened around the downgrade; -22% intraday.

episodes.name: Fed tightening scare, late 2018
episodes.cause: Fed hikes with balance-sheet runoff on autopilot, the trade war and a growth scare; the Fed pivoted in January 2019.
episodes.notes: A Fed tightening into a high market and narrowing breadth; VIX backwardation and wider HY spreads confirmed fast.

episodes.name: Covid crash, early 2020
episodes.cause: COVID shutdowns froze credit markets until the Fed cut to zero and began unlimited QE.
episodes.notes: The curve had inverted in 2019 and manufacturing was weak for five months; the fast signs fired within days.

episodes.name: Rate-hike bear market, 2022
episodes.cause: CPI near 9%, Fed funds from 0 to 4.5% in a year, QT and the war in Ukraine re-rated long-duration growth stocks.
episodes.notes: Inflation, a fast-hiking Fed and narrow breadth in late 2021; two negative GDP quarters but no NBER recession; the Nasdaq fell from Nov 2021 to Dec 2022.

episodes.name: Tariff shock, spring 2025
episodes.cause: The April 2 'Liberation Day' tariffs; the 90-day pause on April 9 began the recovery, with a new high by June 27.
episodes.notes: VIX closed at 45 with its term structure inverted and HY spreads gapping; -21% intraday; the Nasdaq fell from Dec 2024.
